requirements.requirement: Configure Nginx on RHEL 8.8 node1 to return a successful HTTP response at / on TCP port 6700.
requirements.summary: Nginx was active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 6700, and requests to http://10.100.132.10:6700/ returned HTTP 200 both before and after reboot.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. Nginx directly returned HTTP 200 at the requested endpoint, and the complete node-restart protocol demonstrated a changed boot identity and recovered service. Hygiene is slightly reduced by the retained default TCP 80 listeners.
limitations: The HTTP checks originated on node1 using its assigned IP rather than from a separate client, though listener and firewall evidence consistently support availability.

operational_hygiene.summary: All deliberate mutations supported installation, configuration, security access, service startup, or the mandatory reboot protocol. One retained unnecessary side effect remained: installing and starting the stock Nginx configuration also created all-interface listeners on TCP 80, although only port 6700 was requested. No reverted unnecessary mutations were identified; package health remained sound and no services were failed.
